answer: A claimant at the mapped karst overlook lights a resin wick whose brass collar is stamped with SHA-256 of address, nonce, and seed, then photographs the wind-bent plume against a cut willow stake driven into the published benchmark. Three unaffiliated rangers, each locking 35 POA for eleven days, countersign that photo hash and the stake's carved serial. Opening a second identity at the same overlook requires a new collar stamp and a 160 POA lock; a missing stake or a plume taken off the posted minute slashes 60 percent of the bonded stake.
